children: Chemed reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $690.9 million, up 10.6% year over year, and diluted EPS of $5.45. Adjusted diluted EPS increased 28.1% to $6.75. VITAS growth offset softer adjusted EBITDA at Roto-Rooter.
Revenue was $690.9 million, compared with $624.9 million in the year-earlier quarter.
Operating income was $96.4 million, versus $74.8 million a year earlier; net income was $71.6 million, compared with $64.2 million.
Diluted EPS was $5.45, up from $4.46. Adjusted diluted EPS was $6.75, up from $5.27.
VITAS reported a gross margin of 25.4%, up 221 basis points year over year; Roto-Rooter’s gross margin was 50.3%, down from 50.7%.
VITAS adjusted EBITDA, excluding Medicare Cap, was $92.5 million, up 31.4%; Roto-Rooter adjusted EBITDA was $48.2 million, down 2.5%.
VITAS average daily census grew 9.4% to 24,428, while admissions increased 7.2% to 18,995.
VITAS recorded $828,000 in Medicare Cap billing limitations during the quarter. No limitation was recorded for the Florida combined program, and none was anticipated for the 2026 fiscal period.
Roto-Rooter branch commercial activity increased across plumbing, drain cleaning, excavation and water restoration; residential activity also grew across those service lines.

Roto-Rooter reacquired California franchise territories covering more than 12 million people. More than half of the associated revenue is expected to move to company-operated branches, including two planned branches in Sacramento and San Diego; the remaining locations will join its independent-contractor model.
